drafts.title: Foundations for graph-based execution
drafts.body:
## Goal

Establish a small deterministic Go execution engine for editable DOT workflow graphs. Agents do bounded reasoning and engineering; litefactory owns transitions, persistence and recovery. DOT describes graphs with cycles, while Implement will additionally use a story-dependency DAG.

## Starting state

Start in **Research**. This is an independent main issue, not an approved implementation story. Refine this scope through Research and subsequent owner-selected Plan; the child scopes below are candidates only and must not be created now.

## Candidate child scopes

1. Versioned DOT profile, Gonum parsing and validation, registered `lf_<mode>_*` actions and allowed outcomes. No arbitrary executable code in graph attributes.
2. Pinned workflow and role snapshots; durable instance/node/attempt records, outputs, owner-reply correlation and explicit version identities.
3. Deterministic serial transition/action dispatch over existing runner/submission boundaries; preserve provider permissions and selected mode.
4. Restart, cancellation and bounded-retry handling; reconcile uncertain external effects and prevent stale attempts from completing newer work.
5. Explicit old/new execution-path admission and compatibility adapter; active work remains pinned, rollback affects eligible new admissions, never silently rewinds effects.
6. Node/attempt status and traces plus recovery/effect-boundary verification infrastructure. Record token/time baselines without promising unmeasured savings.

Deliver a usable vertical engine slice, not a general workflow product. Later mode parents extend only their required actions. SQL stays in store, time/backoff in daemon, bounded action execution in turn; exact package/API design belongs to Plan.

## Dependencies

None; this is the foundation for the other rollout issues.

## Agreed rollout boundaries

- One editable DOT workflow per mode; registered action names use `lf_<mode>_*`. Start with the standard shipped workflows.
- Pin active execution to immutable workflow/role definitions; bounded loops, durable owner replies, recovery and honest reporting are required.
- Preserve existing permission and result contracts. Users continue to select modes; completing a graph does not select the next mode.
- Keep both execution paths supported until the dedicated retirement. Build replacement team setup before retiring the old setup.
- Coordinate Implement's reduced test scope with Validate's full-suite entry so no testing gap is introduced.

## Origin and scope

Split from https://github.com/marioatcloudvane/litefactory/issues/230 after the owner approved the nine-main-issue roadmap. This issue starts in Research, with 3–6 candidate subissues to refine later. Temporal adoption, a visual editor, a marketplace and a commercial fleet-management service are outside this rollout.

drafts.body:
## Goal

Make Research the first complete graph-driven mode. The reasoning agent assesses clarity within its initial call and goes directly to investigation when scope is clear. Material questions save progress, end the run and resume on an owner reply without keeping an agent waiting.

## Starting state

drafts.body:
## Goal

Replace model-driven orchestration with deterministic story readiness, specialist dispatch and bounded implementation/test/fix loops. This mode has no routine human approval gates. Execute tailored story tests here; move full-suite verification to a coordinated Validate entry path.

## Starting state

Start in **Research**. This is an independent main issue, not an approved implementation story. Refine this scope through Research and subsequent owner-selected Plan; the child scopes below are candidates only and must not be created now.

## Candidate child scopes

1. Approved/frozen-story DAG readiness and deterministic specialist dispatch; default serial writers before optional concurrency.
2. Structured test-specialist recipes: command/arguments, scope, criteria, prerequisites and timeout.
3. Factory-executed story-tailored tests with immutable provenance; no empty/unexecuted check accepted as passing.
4. Bounded diagnosis/fix/retest loops, cancellations and honest exhausted-retry outcomes without routine human approval gates.
5. Engineering completion, dependency release and result handoff without premature acceptance/closure.
6. Versioned change to Implement aggregate-test policy plus resume/failure/conformance verification.

The engine can initially consume existing frozen plans where explicitly compatible. Full-suite movement must be coordinated with graph-based Validate: do not enable a reduced-check default without the corresponding Validate path and versioned contract.

drafts.body:

Run the repository full test suite through litefactory before read-only validation of acceptance criteria, code, architecture and approved-plan compliance. Keep factory test execution distinct from reviewer authority, and preserve the separation of engineering completion and acceptance.

## Starting state

Start in **Research**. This is an independent main issue, not an approved implementation story. Refine this scope through Research and subsequent owner-selected Plan; the child scopes below are candidates only and must not be created now.

## Candidate child scopes

1. Versioned policy permitting factory-run full-suite checks before a read-only reviewer, preserving legacy rules for legacy instances.
2. Repository-declared full-suite execution and snapshot-bound retained results, including failed/missing prerequisites.
3. Read-only criterion/code/architecture/plan assessment using retained evidence.
4. Existing acceptance, reporting and external-effect projection with recovery; no implicit mode switch to fix code.

drafts.body:
## Goal

Retire the old execution engine only after graph execution works across all five modes and required cutover evidence exists. Until this scope completes, support both execution engines, with each active instance pinned to its original engine and definition.

## Starting state

Start in **Research**. This is an independent main issue, not an approved implementation story. Refine this scope through Research and subsequent owner-selected Plan; the child scopes below are candidates only and must not be created now.

## Candidate child scopes

1. Inventory active/pending legacy work and define drain or explicitly authorized migration; preserve retained evidence/readers required by historical work.
2. Establish real cutover evidence across all five modes/providers plus recovery, permission and result-contract behavior; documented rollback/admission gates.
3. Switch eligible new work to graph defaults while pinned active work finishes safely.
4. Remove obsolete execution/orchestrator paths only after retirement criteria; update diagnostics, documentation and compatibility coverage.

2. Verify fresh install, upgrade, pinned-instance recovery and rollback with no dependency on the obsolete setup.
